title: Traffic slicing & canary autopilot for safe rollouts
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Context: As Redwood scales model and runtime variants, we need an automated, observable progressive delivery system that performs fine-grained traffic slicing and canary ramps tied to SLO signals and feature-flag gates. Current manual ramps are slow and error-prone: engineers frequently misconfigure percent ramps, lack consistent rollback criteria, and cannot easily run targeted canaries for customer segments or model variants.

Goal: Build a 'Canary Autopilot' component that orchestrates canary deployments across hosted/dedicated/private modes. Key capabilities:
- Declarative rollout spec (percent ramps, duration windows, and segment selectors).
- Traffic slicing by segment (account-id hashing, region, plan tier, or header flags).
- Integration with feature flags for zero-downtime toggles and per-segment overrides.
- Auto-rollback policy driven by composite health signals (5xx rate, p95 latency, error budget burn, anomaly detection).
- Hooks for staged verification steps (smoke tests, synthetic traffic validation, post-deploy evals).
- Observability: time-series dashboards, per-candidate artifact traces, and audit logs for compliance.

Scope (in): rollout orchestration engine, rollout DSL, console UI primitives for initiating and monitoring, automatic rollback actions, GitHub Actions workflow for gated releases.
Scope (out): model training/CI pipelines, long-term policy engine for cross-service SLO budgeting (future work).

Success metrics: mean time to reach 100% for non-incident releases reduced from X hours to <30 minutes for routine updates; rollback rate for high-severity regressions reduced by 40%; operator time spent on manual ramp decisions reduced by 70%.
acceptance_criteria: A declarative rollout spec (YAML/JSON) supported by runtime router that accepts percent ramps, durations, and segment selectors
Ability to define and apply per-release auto-rollback policies with threshold rules for 5xx rate, p95 latency, and custom metrics
Traffic slicing supports account hashing, region, and a feature-flag override path
Console shows rollout state, progress, and reasons for automatic rollback with links to traces and logs
A fully automated canary run with synthetic smoke test that can promote or rollback without manual intervention
End-to-end integration test suite and a GitHub PR (linked) exercising a staged rollout to a staging cluster

decisions: Use percent-based ramps with minimum step duration (default 10 minutes) rather than fixed instance counts to be cloud-agnostic
Auto-rollback will be enabled by default for P0/P1 releases and optional for lower priorities
Leverage existing feature-flag system as the control plane for per-segment overrides instead of inventing separate targeting rules
Anomaly detection will be initially simple (rolling z-score on error-rate & latency) with a plan to replace it with ML-based detector later
We will not change model versioning semantics; rollout engine operates on model variant identifiers and routing policies
